Issued at 256 PM CDT Fri Sep 25 2026

SYNOPSIS:

A broad upper-level ridge bisected the CONUS this afternoon 
with a trough of low pressure over the East Coast and a digging 
trough over the Pacific Northwest. A subtle mid-level trough was
over the Dakotas east into the Midwest with a stronger 
reflection at 700 mb. Surface high pressure was centered over 
Lake Huron while an elongated surface trough stretched along the
eastern periphery of the Rockies.

THIS AFTERNOON AND TONIGHT:

Low stratus was being replaced by diurnal Cu over the Northland
this afternoon. Expect generally mostly cloudy skies for most 
locations. Duluth, areas along the Lake Superior shoreline and 
portions of the Arrowhead will see the least cloud cover. 
Anticyclonic flow over the region will persist tonight. Low-
level isentropic ascent should be sufficient to regenerate low 
stratus and fog again tonight. The Twin Ports are the most 
likely area to see dense fog Saturday morning.

SATURDAY AND SUNDAY:

The mid-level trough will lift northward across the Upper 
Midwest Saturday as the upper-level trough digs into the 
Rockies. Modest height falls reveal forcing for ascent which is 
also reflected in isentropic analysis over the region. A strong 
southerly low-level jet is forecast over western Minnesota which
will provide low-level convergence and a persistent moisture 
feed. Light rain will develop tonight over western Iowa and 
spread north into central Minnesota Saturday morning. The upper-
level trough will slowly propagate eastward while the mid-level 
trough lifts into northwest Ontario by 06Z Sunday. Rain will 
gradually advance eastward in response. High pressure to the 
east will advect dry air below the cloud layer from the 
southeast which will limit the progression of the rain chances. 
This scenario is similar to what we saw Thursday. Gusty 
southerly winds are expected, particularly in rain, as the 
stronger momentum from the low-level jet mixes down to the 
surface starting early Saturday morning and weakening Saturday 
evening.

Temperatures on Saturday will reach the low 60s (a few degrees 
below normal) near the Brainerd Lakes where rain is expected 
most of the day to the low to middle 70s in northwest Wisconsin 
(as much as 12 degrees above normal).

With the high pressure situated to our east, northeast winds 
over western Lake Superior are forecast to strengthen during the
day to 10-15 knots with gusts to around 20 knots. The favorable
wind direction and funneling between the high terrain of the 
north and south shores of Lake Superior will create a risk of 
rip currents for the beaches of the Twin Ports.

Light rain will advance eastward into the Arrowhead and 
northwest Wisconsin Saturday night and early Sunday morning. 
Forcing for ascent will diminishes as the mid-level trough 
pushes farther into northwest Ontario. Skies are forecast to 
gradually clear from west to east on Sunday. Temperatures trend 
warmer in our west with highs in the middle 60s to near 70 
degrees. The Arrowhead and northwest Wisconsin will be cooler 
due to the slower departure of clouds and lingering light rain 
showers.

MONDAY THROUGH NEXT FRIDAY:

By early next week the trough and cutoff low over New England 
will remain in place with an elongated upper-level ridge 
stretching from the southern Plains into Quebec. A longwave 
trough is forecast to move into the northern Plains and Canadian
Prairies Monday night into Tuesday which brings another chance 
of rain to the Northland. The persistence of the eastern cutoff 
low will result in long moisture trajectories from the Baja 
Pacific into the western Great Lakes. Tropical moisture from 
Hurricane Polo is forecast to slip around the southern periphery
of the Rockies and spill into the Plains and Midwest ahead of 
the Tuesday system. That would set the stage for greater rain 
chances as the trough moves into our area and raise the 
potential for excessive rainfall. Timing isn't quite as 
favorable with the 12Z models which focus rainfall over the 
Dakotas into northwest Ontario Monday night and the Midwest on 
Tuesday. On the other hand, models struggle to handle the 
breakdown of blocking patterns once they are established and 
that could play a complicating factor in rain chances early next
week.

Wednesday and beyond features additional small chances of 
precipitation and near to slightly above normal temperatures.
